content: Hi! I'm just getting started with lean and would love to meet other people interested in formalisation
Hello, I'm a PhD student at the computer science department. Also just started with formalisation.
I'd be curious to know, who in Leuven is working in formalization?

Bart Michels said:

I'd be curious to know, who in Leuven is working in formalization?

It might be just me and Michael, tho I can't find him in KU Leuven "who's who". I am not aware of any professors here that work with formalization, and I'm not doing it for my thesis really, it's just something I'm interested in :).

I'm excited to break the 3-year-and-half-long silence in this thread and announce that we will start weekly meetups in Leuven, in the CS building.

The first one will be on Monday 30 March, 15:00–17:00, in room Prolog (05.128).

Quite a few people I've talked to in the CS department are interested in Lean (both as a theorem prover and as a language for verified software) but don't have experience. So as part of the first few meetings there will be beginner-friendly tutorials, but later we will transition to the kind of regular local event already taking place in other cities.

Come along if you are around!

There will no meetup on 6 April, Easter Monday. The next one will be on 13 April (room TBA).

At the first meeting it was agreed that this series would be named "HeverLean" (after the submunicipality Heverlee where they take place).

The 2nd HeverLean event will start at 15:00 CEST on Monday 13 April in room Python (02.112) of the CS building.

There is also a local Zulip instance for programming languages that could host some Lean-related discussions. If you're local and would like to join the instance, send me a DM.
